Subject: Dedicated sizing help — long context/embeddings mix

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a small internal perf pass over our mixed workload and wanted quick guidance for a Dedicated pilot. Short summary:
- Workload mix: 60% embeddings (short, high-QPS), 35% chat/generation (multi-turn, average 1.6k tokens input, up to 8k context during long retrieval flows), 5% reranking.
- SLOs: P95 latency target for chat ~350ms; embeddings P95 ~70ms.
- Peak concurrency: 420 qps for embeddings bursts (short-lived); steady-state ~60 qps. Chat concurrency ~40 sessions, spiky.
- Cost sensitivity: want a predictable monthly committed cost; willing to reserve if we get a clear throughput fit.

Can you recommend an initial SKU split (H100 / A100 / L4) and any fallback policy we should bake into the Dedicated plan? I attached our sample_query_profile.csv.

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing help — long context/embeddings mix

Hi Sam — thanks for the profile. Quick answers inline and a recommended pilot hypothesis below.

TL;DR recommendation (pilot): 8 x A100 (primary), 2 x H100 (long-context reserve), 12 x L4 (embedding burst pool).
Why this split:
- A100 is the balanced workhorse: good for mid-sized generation loads and offers cost/throughput sweet spot for chat at your 1.6k average input.
- H100 is memory-rich; reserve a small H100 pool to run the 8k context retrieval flows and any large-model evals where KV memory or fp16/quantization headroom matters. You don't need many H100s initially — these can be used as an overflow for heavy context cases and for offline evals.
- L4 is excellent for embeddings: lower per-token cost and significantly better slot-density for short, high-QPS inference. Use as a burst pool behind a routing policy.

Suggested fallback/routing policy:
1) Route embeddings to L4 unless the L4 pool is saturated — then overflow to A100 at a higher per-token rate.
2) Route regular chat to A100. If the A100 latency SLO starts degrading, scale A100 horizontally and temporarily move the heaviest long-context sessions into H100.
3) Canary: start pilot with 70% traffic on Dedicated; failover to Hosted nodes for <5% of sessions during canary windows to validate fallthrough.

Sizing rationale (very back-of-envelope):
- Embeddings: 12 L4s -> handles bursts to ~500 qps with autoscale/burst slots and batching.
- Chat: 8 A100s -> steady 40 session concurrency with headroom for spikes; enable continuous batching and KV prefix caching to reduce token cost.
- Long-context: 2 H100s -> handle concurrent heavy contexts (OOM headroom for 8k contexts, can decode in parallel for few sessions).

I'll run these numbers with Karthik and Priyom to flesh out token-per-second, batch sizes, and estimated monthly committed cost. Attaching a pilot hypothesis workbook (edgewave_sku_hypothesis.xlsx) with initial cost estimates and a one-page ops runbook draft.

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to review the matrix and lock the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park

kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Internal: edgewave pilot — finalizing SKU split and runbook

Team — Sam asked for a firm pilot by 10/29. I sketched the split (8 A100 / 2 H100 / 12 L4) but want your operational checks before I send the proposal. Notes and questions below.

Operational considerations:
- Memory headroom: For 8k context sessions we need H100s with at least 80% memory available after model quantization; recommend reserving those nodes with higher GPU memory thresholds and disabling preemption.
- Tiling and slotting: For L4 embedding bursts we should enable fractional slot packing and a higher max_batch_size (L4 handles higher batches for short inputs). Priyom: can we tune the batching window to 10ms for embeddings?
- Autoscaling policies: For A100s set target CPU/GPU slot utilization at 65% to leave headroom for sudden chat spikes. We'll define scale-up thresholds for sustained 60s above target.
- Cost model: The pilot's committed monthly cost needs margins. I propose a 12% headroom multiplier on top of modeled steady-state token cost to cover OOMs and extra decode minutes.

Fallback mechanics:
- Primary routing table: embeddings -> L4; chat -> A100; heavy_context -> H100. Overflow rules: L4->A100, A100->H100 only for pinned long-context sessions, otherwise fail to hosted fallback (we should limit cross-environment fallthroughs).

Ask: Karthik, Priyom — please review the attached ops_runbook_draft.md and edgewave_sku_hypothesis.xlsx. I need a short paragraph from each of you approving the operational thresholds and confirmation of the headroom multiplier so I can finalize the proposal to Sam.

--
Kim

Subject: RE: Dedicated sizing help — pilot recommendation and next steps

Hi Sam / Alicia — thanks for the patience. Per our internal checks (attached workbook + runbook) here's the consolidated pilot recommendation and next steps.

Pilot SKU & governance (30-day pilot):
- 8 x A100 (primary chat/generation pool)
- 2 x H100 (long-context reserve and heavy evals)
- 12 x L4 (embeddings burst pool)

Traffic routing & failover:
- Embeddings -> L4 with overflow to A100; if A100 saturated, route <2% of traffic to Hosted fallback (cold path) and alert.
- Chat -> A100. Long-context sessions pinned to H100 when detected (8k retrieval flows).
- Canary: 70% traffic on Dedicated for first 72 hours, full cutover after SLA checks.

Operational thresholds we validated:
- L4 batching window 10ms for embeddings; target utilization 60-70%.
- A100 target utilization 65% with 60s sustained threshold to scale up.
- H100 reserved with no preemption and 12% headroom multiplier on compute budget for safety.

Estimated committed OPEX (30-day pilot):
- Modeled monthly committed cost (including margins and burst buffer): see attached edgewave_sku_hypothesis.xlsx -> approx $74,200/mo for pilot footprint. This includes reserved pricing assumptions and our 12% headroom.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: Alicia / procurement@edgewave.ai to confirm budget/PO cadence — we can hand you a DocuSign starter (link below).
2) Kickoff: propose Oct 31 10:00 PT for a 45-minute runbook/ops walkthrough.
3) Tech preflight: we'll provision the Dedicated pools as soon as PO or LOI is signed; we can stage images and test canary in 48 hours.
